Mechanical and Systems Engineering Doctoral Degree
Mechanical and Systems Engineering Doctoral Degree
Ohio University's Mechanical and Systems Engineering Ph.D. program is an interdisciplinary program with specialized tracks in Mechanical Engineering (ME) and Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISE). The program prepares students for advanced engineering work in industry, government or academia.
Through the Mechanical Engineering track, you'll have the opportunity to specialize your research in the areas of biomedical engineering, CAD/CAM, machine and automotive design, energy, manufacturing, materials and deformable solid body mechanics, robotics and rigid body mechanics and thermo-fluid systems.
Through the Industrial and Systems Engineering, you'll have the ability to specialize in manufacturing systems, information systems, artificial intelligence, systems simulation, process planning, distribution systems, genetic algorithms, data mining, location science, supply chain design, human factors and reliability.
Admission Requirements
Note about Fee Waiver for applicants in the Mechanical Engineering track: Applicants with a GRE quantitative score in the 80th percentile or better may be entitled to a waiver of the application fee. Contact graduate chair Dr. Muhammad Ali at alim1@ohio.edu to request the fee waiver code to use with your online application.
M.S. in Engineering: The basic requirement for admission to OHIO's Mechanical and Systems Engineering Ph.D. program is a master of science degree in engineering or related field (i.e. chemistry, physics, applied mathematics, etc.). However, direct admission to the program may be possible if special circumstances are met and granted.
Specialty Areas: Admission is restricted to those students whose educational plans fall within one of the two specialty areas.
The Graduate Record Exam (GRE) general test is required with a quantitative score of at least 161 and 153 for verbal for applicants in the Mechanical Engineering track, and a quantitative score of at least 158 for applicants in the Industrial and Systems Engineering track.
GPA: The requirement for minimum undergraduate grade point average (GPA) is 3.0, and the minimum M.S. GPA requirement is 3.3.
Three letters of recommendation are required from persons who can attest to the applicant’s academic and research aptitude.
English Proficiency Requirement: Please review information about Ohio University's minimum English Language Proficiency requirements for Funding and graduate study.
International Students
This program permits full-time enrollment in residence at Ohio University, and an I-20 may be issued based on admission to this program.

Mechanical and Systems Engineering Ph.D. Course Requirements
A minimum of 60 semester hours beyond the Master of Science (M.S.) degree or 90 hours beyond the Bachelors of Science (B.S.) is required consisting of coursework at the 6000 and 7000 level. Additionally, students must pass the qualifying examination before earning 12 credit hours of coursework applicable toward the Ph.D. degree, and a comprehensive examination no later than the end of four semesters of coursework.
Learn more about the program and view all course requirements on the University Catalog webpage. You can also learn more on the program on the program policies and procedures page.
View Courses & Curriculum in the Official Academic Catalog
Policies and Procedures
Career Opportunities with a Mechanical and Systems Engineering Ph.D.
Ohio University Mechanical and Systems Engineering doctoral degree graduates go on to do advanced engineering work in industry, government or academia. You can find our graduates at leading research universities and companies such as Boeing, Daimler Chrysler, General Electric, NASA, Cummins, and Naval Air Systems command, among many others.

Related Mechanical Engineering Programs
Mechanical Engineering M.S.
If you’re looking for a challenging and rewarding career that will allow you to create an impact that lasts a lifetime, OHIO’s Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering is right for you.
Mechanical Engineering B.S.
Mechanical Engineering majors take courses in engineering, social sciences and the humanities to build their understanding of our technical society.
Energy Engineering B.S.
Our energy engineering program prepares you to work on sustainable energy solutions, evaluate life cycle energy costs and address fossil fuel shortages and effects on the environment.
